description: Conformance corpus for optional bindings and the `xript.has` probe. Every runtime builds the host below from `manifest` and `provided`, runs each case's script in a fresh runtime, and asserts the outcome.
notes: `provided` lists every binding path the host supplies; nothing else is supplied. A provided function returns the string in `returns` (for `echo`, its first argument). A provided namespace is supplied as an object holding exactly its provided members.
`capabilities` is the grant every case runs under. `vault` is declared, provided, and gated by a capability that is not granted, so it pins that `xript.has` answers presence, not permission.

`missingBindings` is the runtime's reported drift for this host: every declared binding that is neither supplied nor optional, nor beneath an optional namespace the host omitted. A host that omits only optional bindings constructs under strict binding checks; `legacy` is the one non-optional binding left out, so strict construction must fail naming exactly it.
An omitted optional binding is bound to `undefined`: the name exists (so a bare reference never throws a `ReferenceError`) and its value is `undefined`. It is never a stub that throws.

`xript.has(path)` is true only when `path` is a declared binding (top-level, namespace, member, or accessor) that this host provides. It is false for an undeclared path, a declared path the host omitted, a path beneath an omitted namespace, and any non-string argument. A namespace counts as provided when the host supplies it, whatever it supplies inside.
`expect.result` is compared as JSON. `expect.error` lists substrings the surfaced error message must contain.

`eagerValue` is a second, separate host. Its `meta.version` is declared as a function but supplied as the plain value in `providedValues` (Rust: a namespace `Property`; C#: `HostNamespaceMember.Value`; JS and Node: a non-function value on the namespace object). The missing-bindings check has never counted that as supplying a function, so it lists `meta.version`; `xript.has` follows that same check, so it answers false for `meta.version` while the namespace itself is present. What the eager value installs as is unchanged and not pinned here.

web.description: Present only where a browser is.

tools.description: An optional namespace this host does provide.

legacy.description: A non-optional binding this host forgot.

cases.name: an omitted optional function is undefined
an omitted optional function is bound, so a bare reference does not throw
cases.script: var seen = share; ['share' in globalThis, seen === undefined]

cases.name: an omitted optional namespace is undefined
an omitted optional member is undefined
a guard falls back when the optional member is absent
a provided optional function works normally
a provided optional member works normally
a provided optional namespace works normally
an omitted non-optional binding still throws when called
an omitted non-optional binding is still installed
xript.has is true for provided declared bindings

cases.name: xript.has answers presence, not permission
cases.script: var present = xript.has('vault'); var denied; try { vault(); denied = false; } catch (e) { denied = true; } [present, denied]
